reason: Harvesting the lettuce directly serves the goal of eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to cut some lettuce leaves for a meal.

alternatives.reason: Watering might help the lettuce, but harvesting seems more immediate for eating it.

effect: The harvest yielded leaves, so I can prepare them for the meal.
reaction: A predictable but welcome result after keeping the plants alive.
reason: Washing the leaves is a natural preparation before eating them.
expectation: I expect washed lettuce, ready to add to the ration.

effect: The leaves are washed and the ration is now offered alongside them.
reaction: This feels like an ordinary, straightforward meal preparation.
reason: Adding the leaves to the warm ration should make the garden meal.
expectation: I expect a meal with fresh lettuce and the warm ration, completing the eating goal.

effect: The supper completed the goal and confirmed that both garden and specimen survived the storm.
reaction: The two fans and covered window make the quiet meal feel earned and link the small action to the larger stakes.

mostWorthwhile.text: The supper passage connects eating the leaves with the protected garden and frozen discovery through the sound of the fans; that quiet payoff made the earlier survival work feel tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Washing the leaves was practical but very predictable, with no additional detail to make the action interesting.

surprise.text: I did not expect the meal to evoke both the garden and the specimen through the two fans; the result made their shared dependence on power vivid.

arbitrary.text: None of my actions felt arbitrary: harvesting, washing, and adding leaves to a ration formed a clear sequence.

continue.text: Yes. The calm payoff makes me curious about what happens after the storm and how the frozen discovery gets home, although the meal decisions themselves were very straightforward.
